summary: US-B5: Order console actions — refund and resend from the console
description:
**As** box-office staff, **I want** to refund an order and resend its tickets from the console, **so that** the full staff-side order lifecycle is available without curl.

The write half of the epic's third COS. It drives **existing** money and delivery protocols (ADR-037 refunds, ADR-038 voiding) from a staff-authenticated surface — it must not invent new money semantics.

**In scope:** a full-order refund action, a resend-delivery action, idempotency on both, a staff-attributed record of who acted, and the role gate on each action.

**Out of scope:** partial/line-level refunds, exchanges (ADR-039 — its own later slice), cancelling an event's order book (TKT-159 owns it), holds management, any new refund semantics.

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] From an order page, an authorized staff member issues a full refund; the money returns through the existing ADR-037 protocol and the order's tickets stop working at the gate per ADR-038 — proven against the real stack, not mocked.
- [ ] A resend re-issues delivery to the order's current delivery address and is visible in the ticket's lifecycle.
- [ ] Both actions are idempotent under a double submit: a repeated action with the same idempotency key produces one effect, and the second attempt is not reported as a new success.
- [ ] A role the matrix does not allow is refused **server-side** with 403 even when the form is forged with the right fields — hiding the button is not the enforcement.
- [ ] Each action records the acting staff principal in an append-only record, pseudonymously (ADR-003) — the record names a staff id, never an email.
- [ ] A refund the downstream refuses (already refunded, gone claim) renders a readable outcome; the console never reports success for a refusal.
- [ ] No new money arithmetic is introduced: amounts stay integer minor units + ISO currency end to end.

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS + gateway smoke suite).
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary; OpenAPI regenerated and committed before the gate (ADR-009).
- UI story: the write forms are **submitted** against the real stack (`make up`), not just rendered — API smoke cannot see the SSR layer (TKT-105 learning).
- Read endpoints declare their ADR-004 TTL tier; auth/session responses are `no-store`.

governingAdrs.why: The gateway is the single public entry point and its route table IS the security boundary; /api/<svc>/internal/ is unreachable from the edge by construction. Anything this ticket adds to the edge must keep that construction true.

Contract-first: a new HTTP surface is authored in the service's openapi.yaml and the generated code committed BEFORE the gate runs — check-generate diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift.
Response drift fails closed: every status code the handler can emit must be declared, or the validator rejects the response at runtime.

The back-office is Astro SSR behind the gateway. `security.checkOrigin` is already false in web/backoffice/astro.config.mjs and form actions must be RELATIVE — an absolute action trips the check even same-origin.
The refund money protocol already exists. This ticket calls it; it does not restate, re-derive or re-implement any part of it.
A refund voids the tickets — refund and revocation are one protocol, not two independent calls the console sequences itself.

Every money mutation flows through the append-only journal and every ticket transition appends a lifecycle event. The staff attribution rides those existing records pseudonymously; it never adds an email to them.
State inside the database cannot constrain an adversary who writes to the database. The staff-attribution record is honest-writer provenance, not tamper-evidence — word the claim that way.

reference.summary: Refund/exchange internal endpoints: POST /internal/orders/{id}/refunds. Edge-unreachable by construction (ADR-002) — how a staff-authenticated console reaches them is the core design question of this ticket.
TKT-116 left a failed compensation refund with no automated path forward (TKT-144) and no operator unpark path (TKT-146) — the console must not pretend those cases resolve.
Refunded tickets still admit at an OFFLINE gate (TKT-162, open) — the console must not claim revocation is immediate everywhere.
